You gotta think of your computer as having separate "zones". The removable storage can have multiple zones via partitioning, one immutable for the LiveCD OS, and another partition for files you can modify. But it's probably best to use your internal HD for large non-executable things (videos, books, zim Web-site snapshots, etc). Read up on how the LiveCD distro you're using is made - there are different approaches to how the different "zones" are mounted into the Unix directory hierarchy.

  • /, /boot, /*bin, /lib*, /usr, etc - the root should ideally be read-only on the read-only boot device. To make updates you gotta roll a new one and reboot.

  • /home, /var, /etc, etc - writable but still small and security sensitive, can be another removable device or partition.

  • /tmp, swapfile - ideally you can store everything in RAM, or could go on the writable external partition.
